topic.original: Under what conditions can the mandatory adoption of siloed datasets effectively mitigate surveillance without disproportionately compromising agent utility? Through what pathways do these architectural constraints—as monitored by independent auditors—alter developer incentives versus end-user privacy expectations? This inquiry interrogates the tension between privacy-preserving data isolation and the pursuit of unified intelligence, inviting stakeholders to question whether such mandates are the optimal pathway for regulating corporate data harvesting.
